items.title: Taxi / MTR to the Lion Rock Approach
items.cost: Urban (red) taxi: HK$29 for the first 2 km, then HK$2.1 per 200 m or per minute waiting until the meter reaches HK$102.5, HK$1.4 after; HK$6 per boot bag; HK$8 surcharge if routed via Lion Rock Tunnel.
items.getThere: HKTB route note: MTR to Wong Tai Sin or Diamond Hill, then taxi up Sha Tin Pass Road to the Lion Pavilion (start of MacLehose Trail Section 5). From TST: Tuen Ma Line East Tsim Sha Tsui → Hung Hom → Ho Man Tin → To Kwa Wan → Sung Wong Toi → Kai Tak → Diamond Hill.
highlights: Sha Tin Pass was the old footpath between Sha Tin and Tsz Wan Shan; the trailhead sits at the pass on Sha Tin Pass Road.
AFCD: a small village store at Shatin Pass sells cold drinks — the last resupply before the ridge.
tips: Say 沙田坳道 獅子亭 (Lion Pavilion) to the driver; a red urban taxi is the right type for Kowloon.
Ask for a printed receipt — drivers must issue one on request; they are not required to change HK$500/1,000 notes.
items.watch: Drivers can legally refuse change for HK$500/HK$1,000 notes — carry small bills or Octopus.

sources.label: Hello! Hong Kong (HKTB content): Sha Tin Pass Road route

items.title: Lion Rock Hike
items.hours: Country park trail, no gate hours. Go in daylight; the path is unlit.
items.getThere: From Sha Tin Pass (MacLehose Trail Section 5) climb west to the ridge (~1.5–2 km, ~200 m gain to the summit), then descend the AFCD-restored stone trail from Lion Rock Pass down to Wang Tau Hom / Wong Tai Sin.
highlights: Lion Rock summit 495 m: the 'lion's head' faces west over all of Kowloon, Victoria Harbour and the New Territories.
Reunification Pavilion on the mid-slope: open views of east Kowloon and the old Kai Tak runway (today's cruise terminal) — preview of the afternoon.
Qing-era stone trails on both flanks were the old Sha Tin–Kowloon routes.
tips: Final 50–70 m to the lion's head is a hands-on rock scramble; stow poles. Stop at the main ridge if the rock is wet.
No water on the trail: carry 1–1.5 L each; the Shatin Pass store is the only top-up.
Emergency: 999 or 112; quote the nearest distance post number (e.g. M0xx on the MacLehose Trail).
items.watch: Ridge is exposed and the scramble is hazardous when wet or windy. Macaques live in the park (mainly near Tai Po Road): never feed them; keep food packed.

items.title: Finish Wang Tau Hom / Tsz Wan Shan Side → Taxi to Kowloon Walled City Park
items.cost: Taxi on the urban meter (HK$29 flag, HK$2.1 per 200 m); MTR by Octopus.
items.getThere: The Wang Tau Hom trail ends ~8–12 min walk from Wong Tai Sin MTR Exit D3 (Ching Tak Street). Taxi from there, or MTR: Kwun Tong Line Wong Tai Sin → Diamond Hill, change to Tuen Ma Line → Kai Tak → Sung Wong Toi, Exit B3, then ~8 min walk to the park.
tips: MTR is a reliable fallback if taxis are scarce: Sung Wong Toi Exit B3 is the station exit MTR names for the park.
Buy water at the convenience stores near Wong Tai Sin station after the descent.

items.title: Kowloon Walled City: A Cinematic Journey (If a Slot Is Free)
items.hours: Park daily 6:30 AM – 11:00 PM. Film-set exhibition daily 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM, 24 May 2025 – 23 May 2028. Since 1 Sep 2026: Mon–Fri 9 AM–12 noon = 2 sessions of 25 min per hour; all other hours = 3 sessions of 15 min per hour.
items.getThere: MTR Sung Wong Toi Exit B3, ~8 min walk. Entrance area: Tung Tsing Road / Carpenter Road. Ticket counter is in front of the Yamen.
highlights: Sets from Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In, installed inside the restored Qing Yamen.
Free outdoor display at the South Gate: bronze model of a pre-demolition Walled City building and a cross-section shadow wall.
Old South Gate remains and Yamen are the genuine surviving fabric; the film set is reconstruction.
tips: Same-day tickets: morning sessions (9 AM–before 2 PM) from 8:45 AM; afternoon (2–7 PM) from 1:45 PM; max 2 tickets per person per collection, first come first served.
Arriving ~11:30 Thu: slots before noon are 25 min; from 12:00 they shrink to 15 min.
Enter at the printed time — late tickets are void; remaining places go to the standby queue.
items.watch: Max 60 visitors inside at once. Closed under Black Rainstorm or Signal No. 8+; reopens within 2 h of cancellation if conditions permit. Staff may shift session start times.

items.title: Walk East: Sung Wong Toi → Kai Tak Waterfront → Sports Park
items.hours: Sung Wong Toi station archaeology display: same as station opening hours.
items.getThere: Kowloon City → Sung Wong Toi Garden (inscribed rock) → Sung Wong Toi station concourse (Exit D side) → Kai Tak Sports Park, 38 Shing Kai Road; MTR Kai Tak and Sung Wong Toi stations are each within ~10 min walk of the park.
highlights: Sung Wong Toi Garden: the 'Terrace of the Song Emperors' inscription, cut from Sacred Hill in 1956 when the hill was levelled for Kai Tak Airport.
'Treasures from Sacred Hill' in Sung Wong Toi station: 500+ Song–Yuan finds (porcelain, tea bowls, coins) unearthed 2012–2015; display renewed March 2024.
Kai Tak Sports Park on the old airport tarmac: 50,000-seat Stadium with retractable roof, 10,000-seat Arena, 5,000-seat Youth Sports Ground (free when not in use).
tips: The garden, station display and park are three separate places with separate entrances — pin each one.
Kai Tak Mall inside the park is the indoor fallback if it rains.

items.title: Kai Tak Buffer — JOYPOLIS SPORTS (Backup Only)
items.hours: Regular days: all floors 10:30 AM – 6:30 PM; 3/F Future Arena to 8:30 PM. Peak days: all floors 10:30 AM – 8:30 PM. Last entry 6:30 PM. Check the business calendar for whether Thu Dec 10 is Regular or Peak.
items.cost: Regular day JPS Pass 60 min: HK$180 (age 12+). Peak day 120-min fixed sessions: HK$360 adult. Grip socks HK$30/pair if needed.
items.getThere: G/F–4/F, Health and Wellness Centre, Kai Tak Sports Park. MTR Sung Wong Toi Exit D or Kai Tak Exit D, each within a 10-min walk. Taxi stand: G/F Kai Tak Mall 2.
highlights: G/F Ninja Dojo: ninja obstacle courses and shuriken laser battles.
2/F SONIC Stadium: SEGA-licensed Sonic sports challenges (incl. treadmill race game).
3/F Future Arena: MR lava game, VR horse racing, AR climbing wall.
4/F Hungry Tiger Hidden Dragon restaurant: 270° views over Kai Tak.
tips: Book online (quotas limited) and arrive 20 min early to redeem wristbands; sign the online waiver beforehand to speed entry.
A 2:15 PM entry on a Regular day gets all floors; after 6:30 PM only 3/F runs.
items.watch: Tickets are date-specific, non-refundable and non-reschedulable. Private events can close time slots — check the notice on the ticketing site. Closed under Signal No. 8+ or Black Rainstorm.

items.title: Early Dinner at Kai Tak
items.getThere: Inside Kai Tak Sports Park (38 Shing Kai Road): Kai Tak Mall 1/2/3 next to the Arena.
highlights: Ming Garden (M2-310, 3/F Kai Tak Mall 2): char siu, suckling pig, dim sum; window seats face Kai Tak Stadium.
So Gor Beef Brisket (M3-107, 1/F Mall 3): signature braised outer skirt; brisket, short rib, tendon noodles.
Gyu-Kaku J (M2-301, 3/F Mall 2): budget yakiniku sets grilled at the table — easy protein.
N+ Burger (M2-102, 1/F Mall 2): Angus burgers in old-Kai-Tak-airport decor.
Food Gala (2/F Mall 1): 10 counters incl. Pepper Lunch Express and JMT Korean — fastest option.
tips: Eat by ~5:15 so you clear security and find seats before your session (about 6:00 PM expected; the ticket time rules).
Food Gala is the low-queue fallback if sit-down places are full before the session.

items.title: WTT Finals Hong Kong — Kai Tak Arena (Ticketed Session)
items.hours: Thu Dec 10, 18:00 = Session 04: Women's Singles R16 + Men's Singles R16 + Mixed Doubles QF. (Session 03 is 12:00 the same day.) Event runs Dec 9–13.
items.cost: Sessions 1–4: HK$880 / HK$680 (CAT 2) / HK$480 / HK$300, plus HK$35 customer service fee per ticket.
items.getThere: Kai Tak Arena (10,000-seat indoor hall), Kai Tak Sports Park, Shing Kai Road. MTR Tuen Ma Line to Kai Tak Exit D or Sung Wong Toi Exit D, ~5–10 min walk; follow signs for the Arena, not the Stadium.
highlights: Season-ending event: 16 top men's and women's singles players plus mixed doubles.
A Thursday evening Round-of-16 session packs many matches across three events into one ticket.
tips: Central side-on seats matter more than category in a 10,000-seat arena.
Bags are screened at the park entrance; check the park-rules page for prohibited items before going.
items.watch: Schedule and order of play are subject to change by the organiser. Session end time was not published on the sources checked.

items.title: Late Dinner → Back to TST
items.getThere: Kai Tak Exit D → Tuen Ma Line towards Tuen Mun: Kai Tak → Sung Wong Toi → To Kwa Wan → Ho Man Tin → Hung Hom → East Tsim Sha Tsui (5 stops). Sung Wong Toi (also Exit D) can be calmer when a session empties.
highlights: Kowloon City's Thai quarter is a short taxi from the park for a late meal (see lunch list).
Kai Tak Mall has 60+ food and drink outlets if you'd rather eat on site.
tips: During major events MTR runs crowd management and adds trains — no need to rush; don't stop or meet up inside the station.
Have Octopus or a contactless card ready before the gates.
items.watch: Taxi pick-up zones change on event days and queue right after sessions; the MTR is usually faster at that moment.

items.title: TST Arcade / Dessert (If Still Awake)
highlights: Verified dessert alternative if you eat in Kowloon City instead: Chiu Chow Hop Shing Dessert (9 Lung Kong Rd) — ~70 years, 90 varieties incl. black sesame dumplings.
Tei Mou Koon Dessert (G/F, 47 Fuk Lo Tsun Rd, Kowloon City): walnut, black sesame, almond and lotus seed sweet soups.
tips: No TST arcade or dessert shop hours were verified in this pass — confirm on the spot before walking far.
Kowloon City is a short taxi or bus hop from the park, so dessert there before riding back to TST is an option.
